was: 100-acre Laurel Highlands campground at 194 Tannery Rd, Champion, between the Seven Springs and Hidden Valley resorts and about 8 mi from Kooser State Park; RV Life counts 230 sites. Under its current owners it is open to the public - the site's own banner reads "RV Sites Available - No Membership Needed" - and is not the membership resort the Roaring Run name once carried. Nightly back-in RV sites with 30-amp electric, water, cable, picnic table and fire ring are published, with monthly and seasonal tiers, rustic cabins from $162 and tent sites also offered. Amenities include an Olympic-size pool, wading pool, camp store, game lodge, mini golf, tennis/basketball/volleyball courts and playgrounds. Satellite shows one large open RV oval of roughly 40 pads plus wooded loops and cabins. Booking is by phone (878-978-2408) or the site's request form; there is no online booking engine. --Claude

was: Privately owned (the operator says so explicitly) 44-acre wooded park at 3075 E 2nd St on US 6 at the top of Denton Hill, 8 mi east of Coudersport across from the State Police barracks - despite the name it is not a county park. 105 campsites including 15 camping cabins; the operator's campground-map PDF shows numbered water/electric and water/electric/sewer drive-in pads (sites 1-105) on two long loops off the access road, plus primitive tent sites, heated bathhouses with private showers, camp store, dump station, honey-wagon service and a rentable pavilion. 2026 nightly rates $35 primitive, cabins $58-128. The operator says it is open year-round (its April 1 - September 30 dates are for the rental camper only); direct access to the state ATV and snowmobile trail systems (ATV trails Memorial Day weekend to the last full weekend in September). Online booking through ResNexus. --Claude

was: Largest of the Lake Wallenpaupack recreation areas, on a wooded point off US 6 at 113 Ammon Dr; the lake and its recreation areas are owned and run by utility operator Brookfield Renewable (formerly PPL), so it is a utility park rather than a government one. 160 tent and trailer sites with camp store, showers, laundry, dump station, playground, marina with rental slips, gas dock and boat ramps. The operator's colour site map classes sites as seasonal, 7-night-minimum, or 2-night-minimum (3 nights on holidays), so a large transient block is bookable; seasonal sites are currently full. 2026 rates $38 tent, 15% off at 30+ nights, 30-night maximum stay. Camping season runs the last Sunday in April to the third Sunday in October. Electric and water reach at least part of the loop (a dated firsthand review reports 30A and water at site 41). No online booking - mail-in reservation form from Jan 1, phone reservations from Apr 25. No pets permitted, and swimming is not allowed within the recreation area. The older wilsonvillecampground.com domain now serves an expired certificate; wilsonvillecampground1.com is the live site. --Claude MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on reservations (7 at some sites), 3 on summer holiday weekends; first-come stays from 1 night (wilsonvillecampground1.com, 2026-10-12). --Claude

was: Formerly Longview Campground, same property at 7570 Robinson Road at the base of Cove Mountain in the Tuscarora range. Operator's own campground map shows 88 numbered drive-in sites - 30-amp water/electric, 50-amp, sewer and frost-free sewer classes - plus lettered primitive tent sites, two playgrounds, pool and pavilion; directory listings put it at 87 sites (18 full hookup, 69 water/electric) taking rigs to 43 ft. Reservations by phone only, no online booking; open roughly May through October, with a Haunted Trail run in the fall. Caveat: the operator's site still carries a stale 2022-2024 winter-closure line and a 2023 copyright, but the park is demonstrably operating - a July 2025 RV Life review describes friendly staff, a clean park, camp store and firewood on site. RV Life ~$38/night. --Claude

was: Large private resort 3 mi south of Hill City off US-16/385 on Rafter J-Bar Rd, backing onto Black Hills National Forest and the Mickelson Trail. 200 sites in six camping areas (Main, Base, Ranch, Lower Ranch, The Island, Line) plus a separate cabin camp: 30/50 amp, back-ins, concrete-pad deluxe patio sites, pool and hot tub, bathhouses and playground. $20 to request a specific site. Online booking was refusing reservations in Sept 2026 ("please call us directly") - phone to book.

was: Chattahoochee NF campground on Cooper Creek in the North Georgia mountains, off GA-60 south of Morganton (Blue Ridge Ranger District); known for year-round trout fishing. Two loops booked together: Cooper Creek (sites 12-25, with 15-16 on the creek) and Mulky (sites 1-11), about 700 m apart. Reservable online; no hookups; no cell coverage. --Claude

was: Chattahoochee NF campground at the headwaters of the Chattahoochee River, 5 miles up gravel Forest Service Road 44 (Upper Chattahoochee River Road) off GA-75 north of Helen. No ATVs, UTVs or golf carts on the campground or the road.  ONLY TWO SITES FIT: sites 15 and 16 are the only ones recreation.gov lets a 23-ft rig book (trailers with no length limit); the rest cap trailers at 10-16 ft or allow no trailer at all, so book one of those two (2026-10-30). --Claude

was: USACE campground on the Mill Run arm of Youghiogheny River Lake in the Laurel Highlands, just north of the Maryland line off Route 40 via Friendsville-Addison Road and Mill Run Road. 30 sites, several right on the cove; flush toilets, drinking water, dump station, beach, boat launch, playground; no hookups. Reservable online; holiday weekends must be booked Friday-Sunday. Site length not published - ring the Youghiogheny project office before bringing a 23-ft rig. --Claude

was: Six drive-in sites strung over about 1.5 km below Alcona Dam Pond; pick 001D, 002D, 003D or 006D (26 ft) for a 23-ft rig. Part of the AuSable River Dispersed Camping system: 102 designated sites along 55 miles of the lower AuSable in the Huron NF, booked as one recreation.gov facility. Dirt or gravel parking aprons; the sites sit on bluffs 5-300 ft above the river and access to the water can be steep. Equipment within 25 ft of the site post; two vehicles and two camping units per site. --Claude

was: BLM (Colorado River Valley FO) campground on the Eagle River just off I-70 Exit 140 at Gypsum: turn south, then right on the frontage road (Old Highway 6) 1.5 miles past the roundabout. Gravel loops between the interstate and the river; a trail leads to the river for fishing and raft access (floating late May-July). Reviewers fit 24-30 ft rigs; the sites further up the road are the better ones. Constant I-70 noise. --Claude

was: Small Forest Service campground at 9,900 ft off Park County Road 60, north of US-285 at Webster toward Red Cone and Webster passes (four-wheel-drive routes beyond the campground). Only the longer parking spurs fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

was: Montgomery County campground in Green Lane Park by the Green Lane Reservoir. Wooded sites with no hookups and no dump station; bath house with showers. RVs to 25 ft. Open April 1 to October 30; book online, same day allowed until the gate closes at sunset; 14-night limit per season. --Claude
note: Montgomery County campground in Green Lane Park by the Green Lane Reservoir. Wooded sites; bath house with showers. --Claude

was: Bucks County park near Quakertown with 17 rustic family sites (no electric or water) by a small lake. Comfort station with shower mid-April to mid-November; dump station for campers. Motorhomes to 25 ft, trailers to 18 ft. Reserve online; 14-day limit. --Claude
note: Bucks County park near Quakertown with 17 rustic family sites (no electric or water) by a small lake. --Claude

was: Bleckley County boat landing on the Ocmulgee River off Porter Road near Cochran. First-come camping for RVs and trailers on the gravel landing - room for a few rigs; pavilion and picnic tables, but no water or restrooms. County ordinance limits stays to 7 nights in any 31 days.  CAVEAT: this is the boat landing itself - no marked campsites, water or toilets; you camp on the open gravel beside boaters' trailers (2026-10-30). --Claude

was: Greene County park near Greeneville on the Nolichucky River (Davy Crockett Lake), with pool, mini golf, ballfields and a boat ramp. About 130 RV sites, most full hookup; showers, dump station. Cash only per a 2025 review; some full-time residents share the campground, so call ahead for a transient site. Pad lengths not published. --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $55 a night, cash, in July 2025 (Campendium review); the park has no web page, only a Facebook page (2026-10-11). --Claude

was: Vernon County's oldest park, in a Driftless valley on the North Fork Bad Axe River near Westby. 10 full-hookup and 7 water/electric sites plus rustic sites; trout pond, 3 miles of trails. Reserve ahead (2-night minimum); April 15-October 15. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on advance reservations; unreserved sites are first-come (Vernon County, 2026-10-12). --Claude

was: City of Montague campground on Business 31 between Montague and Whitehall, across the street from White Lake and beside the White River, the World's Largest Weathervane and the paved Hart-Montague bike trail; an easy walk to both downtowns. No boats or boat trailers overnight in the campground (paid parking in the adjacent city lot, arranged with the manager). About 30 of the roughly 55 sites are seasonal (2024 campground map). --Claude

was: Butler County Conservation area on the west edge of Shell Rock, between the Shell Rock River and a fishing pond, with boat and canoe access, a prairie and a playground. The reservable sites have gravel pads; the first-come sites are on grass and some share an electric post with the next site. --Claude

was: City of Hoisington RV sites in a row along the east edge of the asphalt parking lot behind the activity center (1200 Susank Rd) on the north edge of town; dump station on the north side of the lot. Self-register and pay at the drop box. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $20 a night in July 2025 and May 2026 (Campendium); the city's listing gives no rate. --Claude

was: Small privately run RV park on US-54 (W Kansas Ave) on the west side of downtown Greensburg: gravel pull-throughs behind the laundry building, a short walk to the Big Well. No signage and no website; call ahead. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $30 a night in May-September 2026 (RV Life reviews); the town's tourism listing still says $20. --Claude

was: City of Alma RV park at the edge of downtown, on a rise above the marshy west end of Harlan County Lake; open water is about 1 km south across the flats. Mostly seasonal: on the city's 2021 map 28 of 38 spaces are seasonal and 9 are transient. Wi-Fi is limited. --Claude

was: City of Davis RV sites inside Turner Falls Park in the Arbuckle Mountains, off I-35. About 20 water/electric (50 amp) sites plus some 30 amp, dump station. PLUS daily park admission for every occupant; reservable online. No pets in the park. Very busy in summer. --Claude

was: City of Malin RV park in the Klamath Basin town near the California line, by the city pool. 11 full-hookup spaces, $125/week. --Claude
